studies.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one production game prop for Depths, a dark first-person pixel-art dungeon crawler. Create ONE fallen adult human companion lying motionless on their back, full body from head to boots, isolated on a genuinely transparent background. This is a corpse in the opening escape, fully clothed and dignified, non-graphic, no exposed wounds or organs. Ordinary worn brown leather jerkin over a faded grey-green tunic, patched dark trousers, plain boots, a short muted charcoal cloak partly spread under the shoulders; short dark hair, head turned sideways and eyes closed. One arm bent loosely beside the ribs, other extended slightly away from torso; legs relaxed with one knee slightly bent. Modest single dark dried blood stain on clothing, no pool. No weapons or loose loot. CRITICAL VIEW: strict orthographic directly overhead plan view, as if a camera points vertically DOWN at the person lying flat on the ground. Head points toward the TOP of the square canvas, boots toward BOTTOM; torso centered. The top-down artwork will be laid horizontally on a floor quad and viewed by a first-person camera; do NOT pre-foreshorten, do NOT use isometric or standing front view. Full silhouette with generous transparent margins, body occupies about 85% of canvas height and at most 55% width. STYLE: deliberately simple low-resolution pixel art, designed to be downsampled to a 128x128 sprite; broad crisp clusters, approximately 24-32 muted colors, 2-3 shades per material, no texture noise, no dithering, no individual fabric weave, no fine scratches, no painterly or photorealistic rendering. Adult natural proportions, sober tragic mood, readable at a small size. Neutral material colors with restrained form/occlusion shading only, no directional orange torch highlights, no cast floor shadow, no glow, no floor, no cave, no background, no text, no grid, no frame, no watermark. Deliver one isolated transparent square image.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: ONE second fallen companion prop for the dark first-person pixel-art dungeon crawler Depths. Generate a single fully clothed adult human adventurer lying motionless face DOWN, viewed in strict orthographic plan view from DIRECTLY ABOVE. This is a dead companion in the tutorial opening; sober and non-graphic, no exposed wounds or organs. Full body visible, head toward TOP, boots toward BOTTOM of a square transparent canvas. Head turned partly to one side, face almost entirely hidden, dark auburn hair tied back in a short braid. Simple faded blue-grey wool tunic under a plain worn brown leather vest, dull brown trousers, scuffed boots, a short dull slate cape crumpled behind one shoulder. One arm reaches loosely diagonally outward, the other bent near the head; legs lie relaxed at different angles with one knee bent outward. One modest dried blood stain on the upper tunic only. No weapons, jewelry, loot or detached objects. Subject centered with a broad empty transparent margin; entire body occupies about 85 percent of canvas height, maximum 60 percent of width. CRITICAL: a flat top-down floor texture, body anatomically lying prone on belly, NOT standing or kneeling, NOT an isometric view, NOT pre-foreshortened by camera angle. This texture will be laid horizontally in a 3D cave and then viewed from the first-person eye height. STYLE: simple mature low-resolution pixel art for a final 128x128 game sprite; readable large crisp clusters, roughly 24-32 colors, two or three broad shades per material. Realistic adult proportions, tragic still posture, practical starter adventurer clothing. No individual hairs, weave, painterly detail, soft gradients, antialiasing, texture noise or dithering. Neutral muted leather/cloth colors, restrained local form and contact occlusion only, NO baked orange torchlight or cast floor shadow. Genuinely transparent background with no floor, no rocks, no cave, no glow, no border, no text, no watermark. Keep detail and complexity very low.

note: Top-down studies retained as references; runtime sprites use the final oblique re-renders. No relief mesh ships.
